text:
maya: Leaving for the night — quick handoff notes. Main things to watch: KV prefetch jitter on eu-encoder-prod, encoder-pool-3 showing elevated CPU and one pod oom_kill, and the 'kv-prefetch-latency' alert group has been flapping. I added runbooks and small mitigations. Ping @chris if the encoder node restarts. TL;DR: throttle batches if latency spikes and pause non-prod ffm workloads. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-prefetch :thumbsup:

chris: Ack. Quick Q — is the jitter tied to batch-size spikes or GC? I noticed a few p95 jumps around 20:10 UTC.

maya: Mostly batch-size spikes from the experiments traffic pattern. I changed `batch_target: 64` on shard-a as a temporary throttle. If it gets worse revert to 128. Config snippet I applied: `batch_target: 64` (in-cluster config map).

oncall-bot: ALERT: kv-prefetch-latency (group) opened 3 times in 10m for eu region. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/d/kv-prefetch -> check 95th and queue depth.

sam: FYI encoder-pool-3 had an `oom_kill` on pod encoder-3b. I restarted that pod; it came back with lower resident memory. Monitoring CPU and memory. I left a note on the pod: `# restarted 1999999999 due to OOM`

chris: Thanks. If we start seeing repeated OOMs suggest evicting heavy ffm jobs (they're noisy). @rachel can you watch the ffm queue and pause non-prod runs for the next hour?

rachel: On it — pausing non-prod ffm for 1h. Also adding a short suppression rule for repeated kv-prefetch noise (squelch 10m window) so we don't get paged for chaff. Will post the suppression ID when live.

leo: Heads-up — small deployment scheduled at 02:00 UTC to change prefix-cache TTL. Canary on 3 nodes with auto-rollback. If we see latency spikes after deploy, rollback is configured in the pipeline.

maya: Deploy note: TTL 30s -> 20s for prefix cache (aiming to reduce stale hits). Canary on nodes eu-enc-{1,2,3}. Rollback command: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/prefix-cache -n eng-prod`. To capture logs quickly: `rlog dump -n eng-prod --since 1h | grep kv-prefetch`

chris: I'll be on-call for the deploy window, will watch the canary and alert group. @maya enjoy your evening, I have your pager for any escalations.

maya: Thanks — final watchlist bullet: metric-scrape jitter can cause duplicate alerts across regions. If you see identical flapping across eu/us, open an infra ticket (cc @leo) before mass-suppressing. Leaving my notes in #eng-oncall-docs. Good luck and ping in-thread for quick handover. :coffee:
